The poor oxidation behavior of the as-cast samples is due to the formation of a nonadherent mixed oxide layer (spinel) above the alumina scale owing to the low diffusion of elements through GBs, which fails to restrict the accumulation of cations (M + ) and anions (O 2– ) as reported in few previous studies as well. research_thread.scientific_problem: How severe surface deformation (SFP) modifies the AlCoCrFeNi HEA to achieve superior oxidation resistance compared to as-cast states, specifically the role of microstructural and compositional changes.
research_thread.sample_lineage: As-cast ingot -> Stationary Friction Processing (SFP) -> Ultrafine-grain/Homogenized states (SFP_400, SFP_1800)
research_thread.intervention: Severe surface deformation via SFP at varying rotational speeds (400, 1800 rpm) for 5 min.
research_thread.baseline: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi HEA (BCC/B2 phases, 98 μm grain size).
research_thread.conditions: High temperature oxidation (850-1050 °C) for 100 h in laboratory air.
research_thread.structure: Transition from coarse BCC/B2 to ultrafine FCC with high grain boundary density and nanograins.
research_thread.outcome: Significant reduction in oxidation kinetics (12-48%) and formation of dense protective Cr2O3/Al2O3 scales.
research_thread.mechanism: High GB density facilitates rapid outward Cr diffusion for chromia and inward O diffusion for alumina, supported by enhanced surface free energy.

Elemental homogenization prevents local depletion of Cr, preventing spinel formation (contradicted by observation of spinel).

evidence_spans: In the current work, microstructural refinement of the AlCoCrFeNi HEA was accomplished via severe surface deformation using stationary friction processing (SFP). The processing resulted in ultrafine-grain structure with a significant fraction of nanograins in the as-cast HEA along with significant elemental homogenization. The processed HEA samples demonstrated exceptional oxidation resistance, and the reported mass gain values are among the lowest for the investigated HEA. The remarkable performance of the processed HEAs was attributed to the formation of an intact, dense, uniformly distributed oxide scale, favored by large grain boundary density, higher surface free energy, and uniform elemental distribution.

The poor oxidation behavior of the as-cast samples is due to the formation of a nonadherent mixed oxide layer (spinel) above the alumina scale owing to the low diffusion of elements through GBs, which fails to restrict the accumulation of cations (M + ) and anions (O 2– ) as reported in few previous studies as well. [35] In contrast, the formation of the dense protective Cr 2 O 3 layer followed by Al 2 O 3 inner oxide layered structure in the processed samples is favored by ultrafine-grain microstructure.

The strain-rate (ϵ̇) during processing was obtained using the expression [22] ϵ̇ = R m (2π r / l ), where r is the effective radius of the processed zone, l is the effective depth of the processed zone, and R m is the materials flow rate, which is taken as half the rotational speed in the present study. [22] The strain rate was found to vary from 251.31 s –1 for the SFP_400 sample to 1130.90 s –1 for the SFP_1800 sample.
The high temperature (900–1050 °C) oxidation resistance of AlCoCrFeNi HEA is higher compared to superalloy (Inconel 740 31b ) and other HEA systems. [12] , [13]
